seoTitle: How to Get Stripe API Keys (Live & Test)
metaDescription: Find your Stripe secret and publishable API keys, understand test vs live mode, and learn best practices for keeping them secure.
intro: Whether you're building an e-commerce store, SaaS product, or subscription platform, you'll need your Stripe API keys to connect your application. This guide covers where to find your secret and publishable keys, the difference between test and live mode, and how to keep them secure.

steps.heading: Log into your Stripe dashboard
steps.body: Access your Stripe account and navigate to the developer or API keys section.

steps.heading: Locate your secret and publishable keys
steps.body: Find both key types listed in your dashboard, each serving a different role in your integration.

steps.heading: Understand test vs live mode
steps.body: Toggle between test and live mode to see the different key sets — test keys are for development, live keys are for real transactions.

steps.heading: Copy keys for your application
steps.body: Copy the appropriate key into your website or application code, using test keys during development.

steps.heading: Follow key security best practices
steps.body: Never expose your secret key publicly, and rotate your keys immediately if you suspect they've been exposed.

faq.question: What's the difference between the secret key and publishable key?
faq.answer: The publishable key is safe to use in client-side code, while the secret key should only be used on your server and kept private.

faq.question: Can I use test keys to process real payments?
faq.answer: No, test keys only work in Stripe's sandbox environment and cannot process actual customer payments.

faq.question: What should I do if my secret key is exposed?
faq.answer: Immediately roll or regenerate the key in your Stripe dashboard and update your application with the new key.

faq.question: Do I need to activate my account to get live keys?
faq.answer: Yes, you'll typically need to complete Stripe's account verification process before live mode keys become fully usable for real transactions.
